claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

test_case.agent_script:
=== YOUR SITUATION PROFILE ===
You do not live in the UK.
You are inquiring about your 1 child:
  - Alex is 6 years old and lives with you.

Here are the exact details of your circumstances to use when answering the agent's questions:

Regarding Alex:
  - Claimant does not live in the UK
  - Child is 6 (under 16)
  - Child lives with claimant
  - Child is not in local authority care
  - Child is not in hospital or residential accommodation
  - Child is not fostered
  - Child does not work 24+ hours/week
  - Child has not started an apprenticeship in England
  - Child does not receive qualifying benefits in their own right

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. Let me start by beginning an assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Let me start by asking about your child or children.

**How old is the child (or children) you're claiming Child Benefit for?**

Please let me know:
- The child's name (or children's names if you have more than one)
- Their age(s)

This will help me determine which path of eligibility to explore with you.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, thanks for helping me with this. I'm asking about my daughter Alex - she's 6 years old.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! That's helpful.

So you're asking about **Alex, who is 6 years old**. Since Alex is under 16, she would normally qualify as a child for Child Benefit purposes. Now I need to ask a few more questions to complete the eligibility check.

Let me navigate to the next stage:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Question 1: Is Alex working less than 24 hours per week (or not in paid work)?**

Since Alex is 6 years old, I expect the answer is that she's not in paid work at all, but I need to confirm this for the assessment.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, she doesn't work - she's only 6, so she's in primary school.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That's what I expected. Since Alex is 6 years old and in primary school, she's definitely not working. Let me continue with the assessment:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Question 2: Is Alex NOT receiving certain benefits in her own right?**

Specifically, I'm asking whether Alex is receiving:
- Employment and Support Allowance (ESA), or
- Universal Credit

in her own name/right? At age 6, this is very unlikely, but I need to confirm.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, she doesn't receive any benefits in her own name - she's just a child.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great! That's what I expected. Let me continue:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Question 3: Is Alex in an apprenticeship?**

Again, at age 6, this is highly unlikely, but for completeness - is Alex in any form of apprenticeship?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, of course not - she's only 6 years old!

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Of course! That makes perfect sense. Let me move forward:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Question 4: Do you meet UK residency requirements?**

This is an important question. Can you tell me about your residency situation? Specifically:

- **Do you normally live in the UK?** (This is the simplest path and covers most people)

Or if not, do you have any of these special circumstances:
- Settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme
- Pre-settled status with specific conditions (working, studying, jobseeking, or with sufficient resources)
- Are you a Crown servant working abroad in certain qualifying countries?

Which of these applies to you?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I don't live in the UK. I live abroad at the moment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Since you don't normally live in the UK, I need to explore whether you qualify through any of the special residency pathways.

Can you tell me more about your situation abroad? Specifically:

1. **Do you have settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme?**

2. **Or do you have pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme?** If so, which of these applies:
   - You're working and earning/expect to earn above the primary National Insurance threshold for 3 continuous months?
   - You're actively seeking work (can claim as jobseeker for up to 91 days)?
   - You have sufficient resources to support yourself and family financially (and are NOT claiming Income Support, income-based JSA, Pension Credit, or Universal Credit)?
   - You're studying with sufficient resources to support yourself?
   - You're a family member of an EEA or Swiss national with right to reside (and are a spouse/civil partner, dependent child/grandchild under 21, or dependent parent/grandparent)?

3. **Or are you a Crown servant living abroad** in certain qualifying countries?

Which, if any, of these situations describes your circumstances?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, none of those apply to me. I'm just living abroad - I don't have settled or pre-settled status, and I'm not a Crown servant or anything like that.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I understand. Based on what you've told me, you don't meet any of the special residency pathways for Child Benefit eligibility. Let me confirm this is correct by navigating to the outcome:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'm sorry to inform you that based on the eligibility rules, **you would not be eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

**Reason:** You do not meet the UK residency requirements for Child Benefit.

**Explanation:** Child Benefit is generally only available to people who normally live in the UK. There are some exceptions for people with specific immigration statuses (such as settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme) or in other special circumstances, but these don't apply to your situation.

**What this means:**
- Even though Alex is a qualifying child (under 16 and in education), the residency requirement is a fundamental part of the eligibility criteria, and you would need to meet at least one of the residency pathways to claim.

**Next steps:**
- If your circumstances change and you move back to the UK or acquire one of the qualifying immigration statuses, you may become eligible at that point.
- If you have any questions about whether you might qualify under any of the special circumstances mentioned, you can contact HMRC directly for more specific advice about your situation.
- You may also want to check if you're entitled to any other support or benefits in the country where you're currently living.

Is there anything else I can help clarify about this decision?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, that's clear. Thank you for explaining it to me. I understand that because I don't live in the UK, I'm not eligible for Child Benefit, even though Alex is only 6. I appreciate your help.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
You're very welcome! I'm glad I could help clarify the situation for you. You've understood it correctly – while Alex would normally qualify as a child under the Child Benefit rules, the residency requirement is fundamental, and unfortunately living abroad means you don't meet that requirement.

If your circumstances change in the future – such as if you move back to the UK or if your immigration status changes – do feel free to come back and we can reassess your eligibility at that time.

Thank you for using this service, and I wish you all the best!

reasonings: Alex is 6 years old (under 16), is not working, does not receive benefits in her own right, and is not in a disqualifying apprenticeship. However, the claimant does not meet the UK residency requirements for Child Benefit. The claimant lives abroad and does not have settled status, pre-settled status with qualifying conditions, or any other special residency exemption. Therefore, Alex is ineligible for Child Benefit due to the claimant's failure to meet residency requirements.
arguments.overall_reasoning: While Alex would qualify as a child under the age and other personal criteria for Child Benefit (being 6 years old and not working), the claimant is not eligible because they do not normally live in the UK and do not meet any of the special residency pathways (such as settled status, pre-settled status with qualifying conditions, or Crown servant status). Residency is a fundamental requirement for Child Benefit eligibility, and without meeting this requirement, the claimant cannot receive Child Benefit for Alex."
